newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin wants Russia post-Soviet symbols legalised.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin wants Russia post-Soviet symbols legalised.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday asked the conservative parliament to legalise Russia's post-Soviet flag, emblem and anthem, introduced by presidential decree almost four years ago.

The Kremliln press office said Yeltsin had sent a draft law to the State Duma lower house declaring the tsarist double-headed eagle, the white, blue and red flag and the melody written by Mikhail Glinka in the 19th century and known as the Patriotic Song as Russia's officials symbols.
In 1993 Yeltsin issued a decree introducing the new symbols in place of the red flag, hammer and sickle and anthem written under orders by Soviet dictator Josef Stalin in 1943.

The new emblems are widely used in Russia but they have never been formally approved by parliament, in which the communists maintained a strong position after the collapse of the Soviet Union in late 1991.
The Duma last week debated a return to the Soviet-era red flag and the hammer-and-sickle emblem but stopped short of approving the motion.
